t: #2535 Difference Between Element Sum and Digit Sum of an Array
o: We need |element sum − digit sum| where the digit sum adds up every decimal digit of every number. In Example 1, elements sum to 25 and digits to 16, giving 9; in Example 2 every number is a single digit so the sums coincide and the answer is 0. Constraints are tiny (n ≤ 2000, values ≤ 2000), so any direct simulation works.
k: Digit sum of x is obtained by repeated %10 and //10.
Element sum − digit sum only comes from digits in the tens place and beyond.

a.i: Compute the element sum in one pass, and for each number extract its digits arithmetically to build the digit sum. The absolute difference is the answer.
s: For each element, strip digits with modulo/division and accumulate them.
a.t: O(n · log(max value)) — each number has at most 4 digits

a.i: Each number contributes x − digitsum(x) = 9·(⌊x/10⌋ + ⌊x/100⌋ + …), since dropping the last digit reduces the value by 9 per unit of the remaining prefix. Summing this over all numbers gives the answer directly without tracking two sums.
s: For each x, sum x divided by 10, 100, 1000, 10000.
Multiply the total by 9 and return it.
a.t: O(n · log(max value)) — a few divisions per number

w: Either approach passes instantly; prefer Approach 1 in an interview for clarity. Pitfall: forgetting the absolute value (element sum is always ≥ digit sum here, but stating why is good). Follow-up: what if numbers could be huge strings? You would stream digits instead of parsing integers.
